signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-B-1/2026 (25/03/2026) fines CIB Bank HUF 20,000,000 and orders it to fully meet its ATM installation/operation obligation under Act XVIII of 2025 (ATMtv.) s.2(1)-(2) and s.2 of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI.26.) for settlements over 1,000 population, at the settlements and deadlines in Annex 1. Further breach triggers ATMtv s.2(6) measures and a further fine.
signals.implies: First actual monetary fine under the ATM mandate. CIB missed Phase 1 and is now under a hard remediation order with Phase 2 (>500 population) due 31/12/2026 - immediate demand for turnkey ATM supply, site build and managed services.
signals.likelihood: High - order already binding with dated deadlines
signals.followup: Obtain Annex 1 settlement list (not published in the web version) and CIB's remediation plan; approach CIB with turnkey rural ATM + managed services offer.

signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-3/2026 (25/03/2026) orders OTP Bank to fully meet its ATM installation/operation obligation for settlements over 1,000 population under ATMtv. s.2(1)-(2) and MNB decree 19/2025 s.2, at the settlements and deadlines set in Annex 1; failure triggers MNB Act s.75 / ATMtv s.2(5) measures and a fine of HUF 2m-200m. No fine imposed.
signals.implies: Resolves the previously unverified 'H-KPL-I-3/2026 OTP' item: it exists but is an ATM-installation compliance order, NOT a cash-machine/banknote-validator fine. OTP (largest allocation, 428 units) is behind on Phase 1 - accelerated ATM supply/deployment demand ahead of Phase 2.
signals.followup: Chase OTP's Phase 1 catch-up and Phase 2 sourcing route; confirm whether OTP procures ATMs directly or via framework.

signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-4/2026 (25/03/2026) orders UniCredit Bank Zrt. to fully meet its >1,000-population ATM installation obligation by 30/04/2026 and install an ATM in the settlement named in Annex 1; failure triggers a HUF 2m-200m fine.
signals.implies: UniCredit HU (52-unit allocation) had a single residual Phase 1 gap with a hard 30/04/2026 cure date - small remediation, but confirms MNB is enforcing bank-by-bank ahead of Phase 2.
signals.followup: Verify whether the 30/04/2026 deadline was met and whether a follow-up fine decision was issued.

signals.signal: MNB decision H-KPL-I-2/2026 (25/03/2026) orders Erste Bank Hungary to fully meet its >1,000-population ATM installation obligation at the settlements and deadlines in Annex 1; failure triggers a HUF 2m-200m fine. No fine imposed.
signals.implies: Erste HU (104-unit allocation) also behind on Phase 1. Enforcement wave of 25/03/2026 covers CIB, Erste, OTP and UniCredit - a coordinated regulator push creating near-term ATM procurement urgency.
signals.followup: Confirm Erste HU Phase 1 completion and Phase 2 plan.

signals.signal: MNB decision H-STA-I-4/2026 (24/04/2026), from an ex-officio thematic inspection (case 171861/2025, 36170/2026), finds K&H mis-reported data for Jan-2024 to Jun-2025 in the monthly M01, M04 and M06 central-bank statistical returns; MNB issues a warning (no fine), with repeat breaches exposed to fines of HUF 100,000 up to HUF 2bn or 200% of the annual supervisory fee.
signals.implies: Regulatory data-quality remediation at K&H - adjacent to Printec's compliance/reporting and managed-services practice, though not a core ATM/POS play.
signals.followup: Check whether K&H opens a data-quality/regulatory-reporting remediation programme.

signals.signal: MNB decision H-PM-I-B-8/2026 (13/02/2026), a follow-up on H-PM-I-B-1/2025, fines Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. HUF 5,000,000 (2x HUF 2.5m) for AML/CTF breaches and orders remediation by 30/04/2026 - including a control framework guaranteeing enhanced due diligence for every high-risk client, and system-embedded AUTOMATED IT solutions to support client risk classification, plus effective internal controls for identifying, measuring, managing, monitoring and reporting risk.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Hungary - MNB decision H-PM-I-B-8/2026 (PDF)
signals.implies: The MNB explicitly requires automated IT-based customer risk scoring and stronger internal controls - a direct, regulator-mandated buying trigger for Printec's AML/compliance and transaction-monitoring stack plus eKYC/CDD tooling.
signals.likelihood: High - remediation deadline already passed 30/04/2026, repeat non-compliance escalates
signals.followup: Approach Raiffeisen HU compliance/IT on automated risk-classification and transaction monitoring; check whether a further follow-up decision was issued after 30/04/2026.

signals.signal: MNB decision H-PM-I-B-13/2026 (04/06/2026) fines Raiffeisen Bank Zrt. a further HUF 5,000,000 for AML/CTF failings on beneficial-owner (UBO) identification - failing to verify that the person named on the UBO declaration is genuinely the beneficial owner and to understand clients' ownership and control structures - and orders it by 31/07/2026 to review its CDD practice for closed-end investment fund clients and clients owned directly or indirectly by such funds, build a compliant rule/control environment and re-run due diligence on that population, maintaining a register of them.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Hungary - MNB decision H-PM-I-B-13/2026 (PDF)
signals.implies: Second 2026 AML fine on the same bank in under 4 months, with a 31/07/2026 remediation date on UBO/KYC data - immediate pull for digital onboarding/eKYC, UBO screening and remediation-at-scale services.
signals.followup: Time an eKYC/UBO remediation pitch to the 31/07/2026 deadline; monitor for a third H-PM decision.

signals.signal: Hungary had 5,688 ATMs at 31/03/2026 versus 5,211 at 31/03/2025 - 477 net new machines, +9.15% YoY - with Budapest DOWN 8 units and county seats up only 6, so essentially all growth was in small settlements. Fastest-growing counties: Szabolcs-Szatmar-Bereg +37.37%, Nograd +36.36%, Borsod-Abauj-Zemplen +24.6%. Separately, nearly 1,800 deposit-capable ATMs were operating at end-Q1-2026, +14% YoY, and the total was 5,645 ATMs at end-2025.
signals.source_name: Bankmonitor, 'Hol telepitettek ATM-et a bankok az elmult evben?' (on MNB payment statistics)
signals.implies: Quantifies the mandate-driven build-out: ~477 units/year of net new rural ATM demand, and deposit-capable units growing 14% - squarely Printec's ATM/self-service and recycler/cash-automation lines, plus rural managed services (cash-in-transit-light, remote monitoring).
signals.likelihood: High - Phase 2 (>500 population) due 31/12/2026 sustains the run-rate
signals.followup: Pull the MNB penzforgalmi tablakeszlet Q1-2026 tables directly for the per-institution split and the deposit-capable series.

signals.signal: MBH Bank operates 1,200 ATMs at 1,114 locations (second-largest network in Hungary); it installed 77 new ATMs during 2025 in villages of 1,000-2,000 residents (raising coverage there from 189 to 266 settlements, +41%), replaced nearly 500 ATMs with more modern machines during 2023-2025, and PLANS 115 FURTHER ATMs during 2026 in settlements under 1,000 residents. It met the ATMtv. Phase 1 obligation ahead of the 31/12/2025 deadline. Its 2023 programme targets a 52% fleet expansion by 2026.
signals.source_name: Fintech.hu, 'Tovabb bovult az MBH Bank ATM-halozata'
signals.implies: MBH is the only large Hungarian bank NOT under an ATMtv compliance order and has a named 115-unit Phase 2 programme for 2026 plus an ongoing fleet-replacement cycle - concrete hardware, installation and managed-services volume. No OEM named: identifying MBH's ATM vendor is a priority.
signals.followup: Identify MBH's incumbent ATM OEM and service provider; target the 115-unit 2026 tranche and the replacement cycle.

signals.signal: From February 2026 the statutory free monthly ATM cash-withdrawal allowance for Hungarian household forint accounts doubled from HUF 150,000 to HUF 300,000, still capped at two transactions per month, usable at any domestic bank's ATM and at postal POS; existing declarations rolled over automatically. Average withdrawal size in Q4-2025 was already approaching HUF 120,000 (up ~HUF 10,000 YoY) while withdrawal transaction counts fell by 1.15 million YoY.
signals.source_name: Bank360, 'Nem tudunk megvalni a keszpenztol: februartol 300 ezer forintot lehet dijmentesen felvenni'
signals.implies: Fewer but much larger withdrawals push cash volume per machine up while transaction counts fall - raises cash-out per ATM, strengthens the case for recyclers and optimised cash forecasting/replenishment (Printec cash automation + OptiCash-type managed services) rather than more dispense-only units.
signals.followup: Verify against the amending statute and MNB Q1/Q2-2026 payment data; quantify the cash-logistics cost impact per bank.

signals.entity: OTP Bank / Erste HU / Raiffeisen HU (Constitutional Court challenge)
signals.signal: On 10/11/2025 OTP Bank filed a constitutional complaint at the Alkotmanybirosag against Act XVIII of 2025 and the related MNB decree, jointly with the Austrian-owned Erste Bank and Raiffeisen Bank, arguing the ATM siting and cost-allocation rules are economically unjustified and disproportionately restrict institutions' freedom of enterprise and property rights and discriminatorily interfere with market processes.
signals.source_name: Index.hu, 'Alkotmanybirosaghoz fordul az OTP a kistelepulesek ATM-rendelete miatt'
signals.implies: Confirms the challenge is live and has not stopped enforcement - the MNB issued binding orders and a fine on 25/03/2026 regardless. Banks must keep buying/installing while litigating; a ruling could later reshape Phase 2 scope, so it is the key risk to the pipeline.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no ruling published as of end-Jul-2026
signals.followup: Monitor alkotmanybirosag.hu for the case number and any decision; a strike-down would deflate the Phase 2 pipeline.

signals.entity: Hungarian banks - ATM mandate delivery scoreboard
signals.signal: New ATMs actually installed by each bank over the year to mid-Jan-2026: MBH 316, OTP 128, K&H 92, CIB 38, Erste 36, UniCredit 17. Against the 1,039-unit / HUF 4.156bn mandate allocation (OTP 428, MBH 195, K&H 117, Erste 104, Raiffeisen 65, CIB 52, UniCredit 52, Granit 13, MagNet 13 - HUF 4m per machine). Fleets at that date: OTP ~2,000 ATMs / 536 deposit-capable, MBH 1,200 / 252, K&H 639 / 448, Erste 491 / 260, UniCredit 195 / 94, CIB 156 / 70.
signals.source_name: Origo, 'Uj korszak nyilt a keszpenzfelvetelben - igy alakul at Magyarorszag ATM-halozata'
signals.implies: Explains the 25/03/2026 enforcement wave: MBH over-delivered (316 units) and escaped an order, while OTP, Erste, CIB and UniCredit under-delivered against allocation and were ordered/fined. Roughly 400+ units of the 1,039 mandate remain to be delivered before 31/12/2026 - a directly addressable Printec ATM + installation + managed-services pipeline.
signals.followup: Rebuild the scoreboard from MNB Q2-2026 payment statistics to size the residual gap per bank before the 31/12/2026 deadline.

signals.signal: Consolidated text of MNB decree 19/2025 (VI.26.), in force from 27/06/2025: for Phase 2 (settlements over 500 population, ATM live by 31/12/2026) obligated payment service providers had to conclude the ATM placement/takeover contracts by 28/02/2026 and report each contract to the MNB via the ERA electronic system within 5 working days, with a final reporting deadline of 16/03/2026. Section 4(4) requires a newly designated operator to reimburse the previous operator's demonstrated costs within 3 years. Allocation weights: payment fee revenue 20%, cards issued 30%, consumer accounts 10%, forint deposits 15%, balance sheet total 25%.
signals.implies: Phase 2 supplier selection was legally locked by 28/02/2026, so the hardware/service contracts for the 31/12/2026 wave are already placed or being placed now - Printec must target the delivery, installation, cash-management and monitoring layers rather than a future tender, and the 3-year cost-reimbursement rule creates a recurring site-transfer business.
signals.followup: Request the MNB ERA-reported Phase 2 contract register (likely not public) to identify who won each bank's Phase 2 placements.

signals.signal: MBH Bank completed the largest IT integration in the Hungarian banking market with a four-day bank holiday from 22:00 on 31/12/2025 to 20:00 on 04/01/2026, migrating the remaining Takarekbank corporate and retail customers onto the unified MBH core banking system and new MBH Vallalati Netbank / Vallalati App / Netbroker / Mobilbroker channels from 05/01/2026. The programme unifies systems inherited from three predecessor banks; the migration process closes during 2026, after which the group runs a single core platform.
signals.source_name: Origo, 'MBH Bank: hamarosan lezarul a bank tortenetenek egyik legnagyobb informatikai fejlesztese'
signals.implies: With the core consolidated, MBH's 2026 spend rotates from integration to channel and self-service modernisation - the 115 planned Phase 2 ATMs, the ~500-unit fleet replacement cycle and re-integration of ATM/POS driving and monitoring onto one platform. Prime window for Printec multivendor ATM software, managed services and POS.
signals.followup: Confirm the formal end date of MBH's migration and identify its ATM driving/multivendor software and OEM.

signals.signal: Verified negative: as of 31/07/2026 the MNB's public register of authority decisions lists only five 2026 cash-area (H-KPL-I) decisions against credit institutions - CIB (H-KPL-I-B-1/2026, fine HUF 20m), Erste (H-KPL-I-2/2026), OTP (H-KPL-I-3/2026), UniCredit (H-KPL-I-4/2026), all on 25/03/2026 and all about ATM installation under Act XVIII, plus MBH (H-KPL-I-B-5/2026, 07/05/2026, HUF 15m). No further institution has been sanctioned under the banknote-validator / minimum cash-machine availability regime beyond MBH; no K&H, Raiffeisen, Granit or MagNet cash decision was published in 2026.
signals.source_name: MNB - Az MNB hatosagi dontesei (register of authority decisions)
signals.implies: MBH remains the only precedent for the MNB-listed-validator and availability regime, but the obligations it sets (recirculation only on MNB-listed validators at the exact hardware/software version from 01/07/2026, and a >=98% annual-average availability requirement from 01/08/2026) are sector-wide standards under MNB decree 1/2023. Every Hungarian bank now needs certified validator firmware management and uptime SLAs - a strong managed-services, monitoring and field-service proposition for Printec.
signals.likelihood: High - the 01/08/2026 availability regime starts imminently and 10/11/2026 reporting follows
signals.followup: Watch for the first availability-based enforcement after the 10/11/2026 report; pitch validator-version compliance and >=98% uptime SLA managed services to all nine obligated banks now.

coverage_notes: Full fresh pass on Hungary. Primary-first: MNB public register of authority decisions enumerated in full via desktop-UA curl and parsed locally, then every 2026 H-KPL/H-STA credit-institution decision PDF downloaded and text-extracted with pdfminer. Bank-published MNB decision pages (OTP, Raiffeisen) used to reach AML (H-PM) decisions that are NOT on the MNB kozerdeku-adatok register - this surfaced two 2026 Raiffeisen AML fines the baseline had never seen. Consolidated legal texts checked on net.jogtar.hu (19/2025 MNB rendelet) and njt.hu. Searched EN + HU across regulator, official-gazette, legal-database, bank IR/press and Hungarian financial press; varied entry points vs prior runs (decision register enumeration, bank-hosted decision archives, statute consolidation). RESOLVED baseline flag (b): H-KPL-I-3/2026 vs OTP genuinely exists but is an ATM-installation compliance order, not a cash-machine fine - it was NOT a conflation with the MBH case, though it is also not a fine. Genuine gaps: (1) the Annex 1 settlement lists in all four 25/03/2026 decisions are omitted from the published web versions, so the exact residual per-bank gap cannot be quantified from primary sources; (2) no ATM OEM/vendor is named anywhere for OTP, MBH, Erste, CIB, UniCredit or Granit in Hungarian public sources - vendor identification remains unsolved and is a standing task; (3) no 2026 edition of the MNB Fizetesi rendszer jelentes has been published yet, so the Q1-2026 ATM figures rest on press reporting of MNB payment statistics rather than the MNB publication itself; (4) nothing new on OTP's eMACH.ai core deployment beyond the Dec-2023 contract - the alleged May-2026 contract remains unverified and is again not carried; (5) Hungarian banks are private entities so there is no public procurement trail for the ATM mandate - Phase 2 contracts were legally due by 28/02/2026 and reported only into the MNB's non-public ERA system.
access_issues: kh.hu returns HTTP 403 (Akamai edge block) to both the fetch tool and desktop-UA curl - K&H press releases 'k-h-1-billio-forint-3-millio-befizetes-tarolnak-az-uj-atm-ek', 'forradalom-az-atm-eknel-rengeteg-tranzakciot-erint-az-uj-lepes' and 'bankjegyek-az-atm-be' could not be opened; press mirrors of that material (piacesprofit.hu, mfor.hu) turned out to be from 2019 and were therefore DISCARDED rather than mis-dated as current, so K&H's current deposit/automated-branch figures are unconfirmed and NOT reported. njt.hu/jogszabaly/2025-19-20-2C returned ECONNRESET; routed around it via net.jogtar.hu consolidated text. All mnb.hu decision PDFs return binary to the fetch tool; retrieved with desktop-UA curl and extracted locally with pdfminer.six (pdftotext not installed). Two MNB decision PDFs (Erste, CIB) were located by URL pattern inference after the register listing confirmed their titles and decision numbers.
operator_requests: 1) K&H Bank press releases behind the kh.hu Akamai 403 - needed for current K&H deposit-ATM volumes and automated-branch count: https://www.kh.hu/csoport/sajto/-/sajtohir/k-h-1-billio-forint-3-millio-befizetes-tarolnak-az-uj-atm-ek and .../forradalom-az-atm-eknel-rengeteg-tranzakciot-erint-az-uj-lepes . 2) Annex 1 (settlement lists) of MNB decisions H-KPL-I-B-1/2026, H-KPL-I-2/2026, H-KPL-I-3/2026 and H-KPL-I-4/2026 - request from the MNB under public-data access; these quantify the exact remaining ATM gap per bank. 3) The MNB ERA register of Phase 2 ATM placement contracts reported by 16/03/2026 - would name the winning suppliers for the 31/12/2026 wave.
